02What this is

The Instagram is where most fans first meet her. The profile has to look real at first glance: a real profile picture, her name, a bio, and posts that show her life. Made from the phone's Gmail, never from a phone number.

⚠ The rules that get accounts banned

NEVER CONNECT THE PHONE TO WI-FI. HOTSPOT ONLY.

NEVER DOWNLOAD A PICTURE FROM GOOGLE DRIVE ONTO THE PHONE. ALWAYS OPEN IT AND TAKE A SCREENSHOT.

The apps can see where a picture came from and how the phone connects. Break one of these and the account gets banned.

03Before you start

  • The phone is set up and has its Gmail (SOPs: Setting Up the Phone, Creating a Gmail).
  • The phone is on a hotspot.
  • Her Gmail, password and birthday from the company login sheet. Instagram uses the same.
  • Her profile picture is ready (SOP: Creating Pictures), in Google Drive.
  • Her niche: Star Trek, Star Wars or Lord of the Rings (her model deck).

04Step by step

1

Create new account

Open Instagram. Press Create new account.

2

Sign up with email

It asks for a mobile number. Never. Press Sign up with email.

Why: a number ties the account to a real SIM and to every other account on it. The email keeps each account on its own.

3

Her Gmail, then the code

Type her Gmail. Open the Gmail app, copy the 6-digit code Instagram sent, put it in.

4

Password: the same as the Gmail

Use the same password as her Gmail. Tick Remember login info.

Why: one password per model, already in the sheet. Nothing to forget, nothing to mix up.

5

Birthday: the same as the Gmail

The same birthday as her Gmail (she is 19 or 20).

6

Her full name

Her full name, as in her model deck. Example: Kira Rhodes.

7

Username: her name and her niche

Girly, her name, and her niche in it. Never numbers.

Examples: padawangrace (Star Wars) · kiraofvulcan (Star Trek) · sophieofmordor (Lord of the Rings)

Taken? Change a letter or a word, not a number: sophievalinor, kiraofvulcann.

Why: numbers look like a bot or a spam account. Her name and her niche tell a fan who she is in one second.

8

Notifications yes, contacts never

Allow access to your device: Notifications: yes. Contacts: never. Location: never.

Why: contacts and location link the account to the phone's real owner and to every other phone in the same room. Instagram connects accounts that way.

9

Profile picture

Pick one of her profile-picture-style pictures (SOP: Creating Pictures). Open it in Google Drive, take a screenshot, crop the screenshot, and use that.

NEVER download it from Google Drive. Always the screenshot.

Why: a downloaded file keeps where it came from. A screenshot is a fresh picture taken on this phone.

10

Bio

Short, girly, her niche in it, an emoji or two. ChatGPT can help you write it: give it her name, her niche and these examples.

Kira: just a Trekkie looking for her commander 🖖🏻✨ ♡ cosplay • yoga • Star Trek

Sophie: just a girl who belongs in Middle-earth🌿 still waiting for someone to take me there💞

This bio stays until the account has 750–1,000 followers. Then it changes, to send fans to her link.

11

Skip the rest

Follow suggestions, connect contacts, Facebook: skip. You land on her profile.

12

Day 1 warm up only

Explore page. Tap a post, come off it. Another post, come off it. 5–10 minutes. Never scroll the feed. Never open Reels.

Nothing gets posted yet.

Why: a new account that scrolls hard or posts straight away looks like a bot. A quiet first day looks like a real person.

13

First posts: after 24 hours of warm up

Not before. After 24 hours of warm up, post her first pictures: lifestyle posts and carousels, so the profile has life. This is a new account after its first 4 posts:

Kira: a new account after its first 4 posts. Profile picture, full name, niche username, bio.

05What the profile should look like

When it's been running a while. Open it as if you were a fan: would you believe she's real? Ignore the follower numbers; look at the picture, the name, the bio and the grid.

Sophie: a running account. Her face, her niche, her life, pinned posts, reels and highlights.

06Done means

  • Made with her Gmail, no phone number.
  • Same password and birthday as the Gmail.
  • Her full name, a niche username with no numbers, a bio.
  • A profile picture from a screenshot, never a download.
  • Notifications on, contacts never.
  • The username is in the company login sheet.
  • Day 1 warm up done. No posts until 24 hours of warm up.

07Common mistakes

  • Signing up with a phone number. Always the email.
  • Numbers in the username.
  • Downloading the picture from Drive instead of a screenshot.
  • Allowing contacts.
  • Posting before 24 hours of warm up.
  • Scrolling or opening Reels on day 1.
